Ui.Script:
-- The five windows' shared slot count cap: the backpack is always exactly 16 -- (GetContainerNumSlots(0) never varies — PACK_SLOTS is a wire constant); the -- equipped-bag windows show up to this many (5 rows × 4 columns — the reference template's -- true max is 36, but 20 is vanilla's largest actual equippable bag, and building out to 36 -- slot buttons per window for content that can never exist would be pure waste. Hides the -- unused tail via BenillaBagSlot_Update's physIndex-past-size branch, same as the backpack. BENILLA_BAG_WINDOW_MAX_SLOTS = 20
-- The keyring's container id (ref MainMenuBarBagButtons.lua:1) — decision 0765. It is an -- ordinary container in every respect the seam cares about: the app feeds it like any other -- bag (its slots are the player descriptor's own 81.., no container object), and every -- container verb, the cursor, the pending-op lock and the wire drains take it unchanged. -- What makes it special is only what the reference makes special: the window's art, its -- open/close sound, and the fact that its capacity is not a wire field. KEYRING_CONTAINER = -2
-- The keyring's usable slot count (ref GetKeyRingSize, ContainerFrame.lua:773). The -- reference recomputes a level ladder in Lua (4 / 8 at 40 / 12 at 50 / 16 above 60) that the -- server enforces identically (Player::GetMaxKeyringSize); benilla computes it once app-side -- and feeds it as the container's own size, so this reads it back rather than keeping a -- second copy of the ladder that could drift from the one the feed uses. function GetKeyRingSize() return GetContainerNumSlots(KEYRING_CONTAINER) end
-- BenillaBagSlot_OnLoad(button, physIndex): physIndex is the button's CHAIN position (1 = -- bottom-right, growing up-and-left — the anchor order below), not the game slot. The ref's -- own formula (index = size - j + 1, ContainerFrame.lua:426/446) maps chain position → game -- slot dynamically in BenillaBagSlot_Update, so slot 1 always reads top-left regardless of -- how many of the window's slots are actually occupied — recomputed every Update (the ref -- only computes it once, at window generation; recomputing is a strict robustness win for -- the rare live bag-swap case, not a behavior change for a size that never moves). function BenillaBagSlot_OnLoad(button, physIndex) button.physIndex = physIndex button.icon = getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Icon") button.count = getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Count") -- Both buttons must reach OnClick (the default set is LeftButtonUp only): LEFT-click is the -- pickup gesture (PickupContainerItem — pick up / place / swap on the cursor); RIGHT-click -- cancels a held cursor, else uses the slot (the C side sells it when a merchant is open — -- our container drain forks). button:RegisterForClicks("LeftButtonUp", "RightButtonUp") -- The drag trio (decision 0216 §3): click-carry and drag are ONE code path in the -- reference (ContainerFrame.xml:40-55 routes OnDragStart/OnReceiveDrag to the same -- OnClick("LeftButton", ignoreModifiers=1) the plain click uses) — see -- BenillaBagSlot_OnClick below for the identical routing (its own `ignoreModifiers` -- suppresses the shift-split fork, the reference's own contract for drag/receive). button:RegisterForDrag("LeftButton") BenillaBagSlot_Update(button) end
function BenillaBagSlot_OnClick(button, mouseButton, ignoreModifiers) if button.slot == nil then return end -- a hidden button (physIndex past the bag's size) local bagId = button:GetParent():GetID() if mouseButton == "LeftButton" then -- The reference's own five returns (ContainerFrame.lua:241) — decision 1199 -- put this binding back on its 1.12 shape. local texture, itemCount, locked, quality, readable = GetContainerItemInfo(bagId, button.slot) -- The modifier fork, the reference's own order (ContainerFrame.lua:563-579; -- BankFrame.lua:141-152 for a bank slot, which is this same handler at container -- -1). `ignoreModifiers` (the drag-trio calls, both true) suppresses it whole — -- the reference's drag/receive contract. -- -- CTRL: preview the item on your own character in the dressing room (decision 1060). if IsControlKeyDown() and not ignoreModifiers then DressUpItemLink(GetContainerItemLink(bagId, button.slot)) return end -- SHIFT: post the item's link into the chat edit box if it's open, ELSE split the -- stack. The ref's own `else` (l.567-577) — and note it gates on `IsShown()` here -- where its siblings use `IsVisible()`; ours are the same thing (the edit box's only -- parent is UIParent), so the ref's own word is quoted at each site. if IsShiftKeyDown() and not ignoreModifiers then -- The visibility test is the REF'S fork, not the helper's: with chat open this -- arm never splits, even in the one benilla state where nothing can be posted -- (an unresolved template — `BenillaChatEdit_InsertLink`'s own note). if ChatFrameEditBox and ChatFrameEditBox:IsShown() then BenillaChatEdit_InsertLink(GetContainerItemLink(bagId, button.slot)) return end if texture ~= nil and not locked and (itemCount or 1) >= 2 then button.SplitStack = function(btn, n) SplitContainerItem(bagId, btn.slot, n) BenillaBagWindow_Repaint(btn:GetParent()) end -- Ref ContainerFrameItemButton_OnLoad/_OnClick (ContainerFrame.lua:558-560, -- 573-576): the owner's own SplitStack closure carries the bag/slot so -- StackSplitFrameOkay_Click's generic `owner.SplitStack(owner, split)` call -- needs no window-specific knowledge. SplitContainerItem lives in cursor.rs -- rather than container.rs — it is the one container-named verb whose -- payload is the cursor's, not a bag's — but like every container verb it is -- a plain top-level global (decision 1198). OpenStackSplitFrame(itemCount, button, "BOTTOMRIGHT", "TOPRIGHT") end return end -- A plain click hides any open split frame (ref ContainerFrame.lua:581) before the -- ordinary pickup/place proceeds. local split = getglobal("StackSplitFrame") if split then split:Hide() end -- PickupContainerItem is the single drag entry point (real client): an empty cursor -- picks this slot up; a held cursor places/swaps into it (same slot = cancel). Hide the -- hover tooltip (the item just left the slot for the cursor) and repaint so the picked -- slot dims / un-dims immediately — the swap itself settles when the server answers. PickupContainerItem(bagId, button.slot) GameTooltip:Hide() BenillaBagWindow_Repaint(button:GetParent()) elseif mouseButton == "RightButton" then -- A held cursor cancels (client-side, nothing sent); otherwise use/equip/sell the slot. if CursorHasItem() then ClearCursor() BenillaBagWindow_Repaint(button:GetParent()) else UseContainerItem(bagId, button.slot) end end end
-- Hover: the era-true GameTooltip:SetBagItem(bag, slot) — the ENGINE renders the full -- item tooltip from the template store and owns the sell-price money law (real instance -- + merchant open + repair off ⇒ OnTooltipAddMoney(SellPrice × stack), or the -- ITEM_UNSELLABLE line — wow-re ui/scratch/tooltip-money.md's byte-verified gate, -- decision 0274 P1). The durability-adjusted damaged price is deferred until durability -- damage reaches the feed (a pristine item reduces to SellPrice × stack, the case we -- ship). Nothing shows while the template is in flight — the OnUpdate re-enter fills it. function BenillaBagSlot_OnEnter(button) if button.slot == nil then return end local bagId = button:GetParent():GetID() local texture, itemCount, locked, quality, readable = GetContainerItemInfo(bagId, button.slot) -- An emptied slot drops its tooltip (ref ContainerFrame_Update's texture-nil branch, -- ContainerFrame.lua:281-283) — without this the OnUpdate re-enter below would leave -- a stale tooltip up after the item is sold or moved out from under the hover. if not texture then if GameTooltip:IsOwned(button) then GameTooltip:Hide() end return end -- Ref ContainerFrameItemButton_OnEnter (ContainerFrame.lua:602-612) verbatim: a slot -- in the RIGHT half of the screen hangs its tooltip LEFT, so it never runs off the -- edge (the bag lives at the bottom-right — this is the ref's own screen-edge answer, -- a side-pick, not a clamp). if (button:GetRight() or 0) >= (GetScreenWidth() / 2) then GameTooltip:SetOwner(button, "ANCHOR_LEFT") else GameTooltip:SetOwner(button, "ANCHOR_RIGHT") end GameTooltip:SetBagItem(bagId, button.slot) -- The pouch/magnifier cursor (ref ContainerFrameItemButton_OnEnter tail, -- ContainerFrame.lua l.636-642): merchant open on the MERCHANT tab and not repair -- mode → the sell cursor over this slot; else a readable item (a mail letter copy — -- right-click opens the reader) → the Inspect magnifier; anything else restores the -- base cursor. The OnUpdate re-enter keeps it current while hovering (the ref's own -- loop). The ref's `IsControlKeyDown() and hasItem` magnifier arm (l.638) is the -- dress-up preview's own cursor tell — it landed with the dressing room (decision -- 1060); `info` is non-nil above, which is the ref's `hasItem`. if MerchantFrame and MerchantFrame:IsShown() and MerchantFrame.selectedTab == 1 and not InRepairMode() then ShowContainerSellCursor(bagId, button.slot) elseif readable or IsControlKeyDown() then ShowInspectCursor() else ResetCursor() end GameTooltip:Show() end
function BenillaBagSlot_OnLeave(button) GameTooltip:Hide() -- Ref ItemButton OnLeave (ContainerFrame.xml): the hover's sell cursor drops with it. ResetCursor() end
-- Ref ContainerFrameItemButton_OnUpdate (ContainerFrame.lua:645-660): while the tooltip -- is ours, re-run OnEnter every frame — the ref ships this loop UNTHROTTLED (its -- updateTooltip throttle is commented out in 1.12). It is the real client's own refresh -- mechanism: a tooltip set while the item template was still in flight fills itself in -- the moment the answer lands, no re-hover. function BenillaBagSlot_OnUpdate(button) if GameTooltip:IsOwned(button) then BenillaBagSlot_OnEnter(button) end end
-- The item's use-cooldown sweep (ref ContainerFrame_UpdateCooldown, -- ContainerFrame.lua:295-299, verbatim shape over our container dialect). function BenillaBagSlot_UpdateCooldown(button, bagId) local cooldown = getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Cooldown") local start, duration, enable = GetContainerItemCooldown(bagId, button.slot) CooldownFrame_SetTimer(cooldown, start, duration, enable) end
-- The physIndex → game-slot resolution (the module doc above) + the paint (ref -- ContainerFrame_Update, ContainerFrame.lua:234-293). Shared by every window's slot -- buttons. The occupied/empty fork drives the cooldown exactly as the ref does -- (l.248-253: occupied → UpdateCooldown, empty → Cooldown:Hide()). function BenillaBagSlot_Update(button) local bagId = button:GetParent():GetID() local size = GetContainerNumSlots(bagId) if button.physIndex > size then button.slot = nil button:Hide() return end button.slot = size - button.physIndex + 1 button:Show() local texture, itemCount, locked = GetContainerItemInfo(bagId, button.slot) if texture ~= nil or itemCount ~= nil then BenillaBagSlot_UpdateCooldown(button, bagId) button.icon:SetTexture(texture or BENILLA_FALLBACK_ICON) -- A locked slot (its item is up on the cursor, or a send is still pending -- server-side, decision 0216 §4/0218 §3) dims, the real client's drag feedback. if locked then button.icon:SetVertexColor(0.4, 0.4, 0.4) else button.icon:SetVertexColor(1, 1, 1) end if (itemCount or 1) > 1 then button.count:SetText(itemCount) else button.count:SetText("") end else button.icon:SetTexture(nil) button.count:SetText("") getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Cooldown"):Hide() end end
-- The generic per-window repaint (decision 0216 slice 2): every slot up to this window's -- cap, the title (GetBagName — dynamic since a live bag swap changes it), and the money -- purse (backpack only, ContainerFrame.lua l.314). BenillaBagFrame_Update (below) is the -- backpack's zero-arg convenience alias, kept for existing callers (UiPanels.xml's -- OpenBackpack/CloseBackpack, and the tests that patch it directly). function BenillaBagWindow_Update(frame) local bagId = frame:GetID() local maxSlots = (bagId == 0) and 16 or BENILLA_BAG_WINDOW_MAX_SLOTS -- The backpack predates the $parent-prefixed slot naming (BenillaBagSlot1..16, not -- BenillaBagFrameSlot1..16 — its buttons are hand-authored, not $parent-templated) and -- several existing tests reference that exact name directly; every other window's slots -- DO follow frame:GetName().."Slot"..i (the virtual template's $parentSlotN). local slotPrefix = (bagId == 0) and "BenillaBagSlot" or (frame:GetName() .. "Slot") for i = 1, maxSlots do local button = getglobal(slotPrefix .. i) if button then BenillaBagSlot_Update(button) end end local title = getglobal(frame:GetName() .. "Name") if title then -- The keyring is titled from the localized KEYRING string, not GetBagName — it has -- no bag ITEM to be named after (ref ContainerFrame.lua l.418). if bagId == KEYRING_CONTAINER then title:SetText(KEYRING) else title:SetText(GetBagName(bagId) or "") end end if bagId == 0 then BenillaMoney_Set("BenillaBagMoney", GetMoney()) elseif bagId == KEYRING_CONTAINER then -- Fixed art, again because there is no bag item: the keyring's own portrait -- (ref ContainerFrame.lua l.419) and its own background variant, snug-fitted to the -- level-gated slot count exactly like an equipped bag. local portrait = getglobal(frame:GetName() .. "Portrait") if portrait then portrait:SetPortraitToTexture("Interface\\ContainerFrame\\KeyRing-Bag-Icon") end local size = GetContainerNumSlots(bagId) if size > 0 then BenillaBagWindow_FitBackground(frame, size) end else -- The window's portrait is the bag's OWN item icon (the real client's -- C-side SetBagPortaitTexture), not the default backpack art. An equipped bag -- (1..4) reads its doll slot (19+bagId, Bag0Slot..Bag3Slot); a bank bag (5..10, -- decision 0604) reads the app-resolved bank-bag feed instead — the doll array -- stops at the equipped bags, so GetInventoryItemTexture can't reach the vault's. -- Falls back to the backpack icon while the item template's icon is in flight. local portrait = getglobal(frame:GetName() .. "Portrait") if portrait then local icon if bagId >= 5 then icon = BenillaGetBankBagTexture(bagId - 4) else icon = GetInventoryItemTexture("player", 19 + bagId) end if icon then -- The circular crop (the real SetBagPortaitTexture is C-side and masks the -- icon to the ring's inscribed circle): a raw square icon pokes its corners -- past the round rim — the director's bank-bag popout artifact. portrait:SetPortraitToTexture(icon) else -- The backpack fallback art is authored round — no crop to apply. portrait:SetTexture("Interface\\Buttons\\Button-Backpack-Up") end end -- Equipped bags snug-fit their stitched background to the live row count. local size = GetContainerNumSlots(bagId) if size > 0 then BenillaBagWindow_FitBackground(frame, size) end end end
-- Fit an equipped-bag window's stitched background (BgTop/BgMiddle/BgBottom, authored in the -- template above) and its OWN height to the bag's actual row count. This is a transcription of -- the real client's ContainerFrame_GenerateFrame (the id~=0 branch) as shipped in the 1.12.1 -- MPQ (Interface\FrameXML\ContainerFrame.lua) — every constant below is the reference's, not a -- measured approximation. rows = ceil(size/4). The TOP piece carries the header + the first -- well row; the MIDDLE tiles the remaining rows; the BOTTOM is the frame's bottom rim. The -- slot buttons anchor UP from the frame's BOTTOMRIGHT (first at -12,9) and hide past `size` -- (BenillaBagSlot_Update), so nothing here touches them — only the art + the frame height. -- Which UI-Bag-Components variant a window is stitched from — the ref's own `bagTextureSuffix` -- (ContainerFrame_GenerateFrame, ContainerFrame.lua l.326-334): the bank bags get the -- tinted "-Bank" plate, the keyring the "-Keyring" one, an equipped bag the plain sheet. -- All three atlases are 256x512 with the same band layout, so FitBackground's tex-coords -- are shared verbatim and only the file differs. (Ours ALSO applies the "-Bank" arm, which -- benilla had been quietly skipping — the bank popouts have been drawing ordinary bag art -- since decision 0604.) function BenillaBagWindow_BgTexture(bagId) local suffix = "" if bagId >= 5 then suffix = "-Bank" elseif bagId == KEYRING_CONTAINER then suffix = "-Keyring" end return "Interface\\ContainerFrame\\UI-Bag-Components" .. suffix end
function BenillaBagWindow_FitBackground(frame, size) local name = frame:GetName() local top = getglobal(name .. "BgTop") local middle = getglobal(name .. "BgMiddle") local bottom = getglobal(name .. "BgBottom") if not (top and middle and bottom) then return end -- Re-set every fit, as the ref does at every generate: the template authors the plain -- sheet, and a window's kind is only known from its id. local bg = BenillaBagWindow_BgTexture(frame:GetID()) top:SetTexture(bg) middle:SetTexture(bg) bottom:SetTexture(bg) local rowH = 41 -- rowHeight local rows = math.ceil(size / 4) if rows < 1 then rows = 1 end -- isPlusTwoBag: a size leaving a remainder of 2 (6/10/14/18) has a 2-well top row, and the -- texture carries a whole separate top band for it. local plusTwo = (size - math.floor(size / 4) * 4) == 2 local topH if plusTwo then topH = 72 top:SetTexCoord(0, 1, 0.189453125, 0.330078125) elseif rows == 1 then topH = 86 -- one row only: chop the bottom of the texture top:SetTexCoord(0, 1, 0.00390625, 0.16796875) else topH = 94 top:SetTexCoord(0, 1, 0.00390625, 0.18359375) end top:SetHeight(topH) -- The top piece already carries one row, so the middle tiles `rows - 1` more. Its height is -- one row short of a clean multiple: the reference's firstRowPixelOffset = 9 accounts for -- the 9px the BOTTOM rim itself contributes to the final row's frame. Getting this wrong -- pushes the rim a row-fraction too low and bleeds the NEXT row's wells in above it. local middleH = 0 bottom:ClearAllPoints() if rows > 1 then -- A single middle piece spans at most ROWS_IN_BG_TEXTURE (6) rows; the reference -- cycles up to MAX_BG_TEXTURES for windows taller than that. Our largest window is a -- 20-slot bag (4 middle rows) and the keyring caps at 16 (3), so one always suffices. middleH = (rows - 1) * rowH - 9 middle:SetHeight(middleH) middle:SetTexCoord(0, 1, 0.353515625, middleH / 512 + 0.353515625) middle:Show() bottom:SetPoint("TOPRIGHT", middle, "BOTTOMRIGHT", 0, 0) else -- One row: the rim seats straight under the top piece. (The reference anchors it to the -- hidden middle's TOP, which is the same point — the middle hangs off the top's bottom.) middle:Hide() bottom:SetPoint("TOPRIGHT", top, "BOTTOMRIGHT", 0, 0) end -- The bottom rim is a FIXED 10px band at texture v 0.330078125..0.349609375 — the strip -- immediately below the plus-two top band, and the only true outer bottom border in the -- texture. The reference never rescales or re-coords it; it is authored once in XML. local bottomH = 10 bottom:SetHeight(bottomH) bottom:SetTexCoord(0, 1, 0.330078125, 0.349609375) frame:SetHeight(topH + middleH + bottomH) -- A live size change (a bag swap while the stack is open) shifts every window stacked above -- this one; re-run the stack layout so they re-seat against the new height. if frame:IsShown() then BenillaBagStack_Relayout() end end
function BenillaBagFrame_Update() BenillaBagWindow_Update(BenillaBagFrame) end
-- Routes a repaint through the backpack's own zero-arg BenillaBagFrame_Update alias when -- `frame` IS the backpack — preserving that global's observability (existing tests patch it -- directly to count backpack repaints, e.g. delete_item_tests.rs's stuck-darkening -- regression check) — and BenillaBagWindow_Update generically for every other window. Every -- runtime repaint trigger (a slot click, an event, OpenAllBags' pre-show paint) goes -- through this; BenillaBagBarSlot_OnClick calls BenillaBagWindow_Update directly (it only ever -- targets bags 1..4). function BenillaBagWindow_Repaint(frame) if frame:GetID() == 0 then BenillaBagFrame_Update() else BenillaBagWindow_Update(frame) end end
-- OnLoad/OnEvent (generic, shared by all five windows — each already receives `frame`, so -- deriving bagId from `frame:GetID()` needs no per-window body). function BenillaBagFrame_OnLoad(frame) frame:RegisterEvent("BAG_UPDATE") -- The engine fires ITEM_LOCK_CHANGED(bag, slot) on every cursor pickup/clear AND every -- pending-op send/resolve (decisions 0216 §4/0218 §3) — including clears the bag never -- clicked through (the delete popup's No, ESC; a server failure), which the click-time -- repaint can't see. The reference ContainerFrame repaints on exactly this event. frame:RegisterEvent("ITEM_LOCK_CHANGED") -- Item cooldown starts/ends (ref ContainerFrame_OnLoad, ContainerFrame.lua:21 — -- BAG_UPDATE_COOLDOWN carries no bag argument; every open window refreshes). frame:RegisterEvent("BAG_UPDATE_COOLDOWN") -- The real backpack MoneyFrame refreshes on PLAYER_MONEY (SmallMoneyFrame's own OnEvent); -- keep the purse live while the window is open. Backpack only — the other windows never -- show a purse, so there's nothing for them to refresh. if frame:GetID() == 0 then frame:RegisterEvent("PLAYER_MONEY") end end
function BenillaBagFrame_OnEvent(frame) if event == "PLAYER_MONEY" then BenillaMoney_Set("BenillaBagMoney", GetMoney()) return end -- The cooldown-only refresh (ref ContainerFrame_UpdateCooldowns via OnEvent, -- ContainerFrame.lua:243-253's loop shape): no bag argument — sweep every shown -- slot of THIS window, no full repaint. if event == "BAG_UPDATE_COOLDOWN" then local bagId = frame:GetID() local maxSlots = (bagId == 0) and 16 or BENILLA_BAG_WINDOW_MAX_SLOTS local slotPrefix = (bagId == 0) and "BenillaBagSlot" or (frame:GetName() .. "Slot") for i = 1, maxSlots do local button = getglobal(slotPrefix .. i) if button and button.slot then BenillaBagSlot_UpdateCooldown(button, bagId) end end return end -- BAG_UPDATE / ITEM_LOCK_CHANGED name their bag in arg1; only THIS window's own bag -- repaints (ref ContainerFrame_OnEvent, ContainerFrame.lua:26-44: `this:GetID() == arg1`). if (event == "BAG_UPDATE" or event == "ITEM_LOCK_CHANGED") and arg1 ~= frame:GetID() then return end BenillaBagWindow_Repaint(frame) end
-- OpenAllBags / CloseAllBags / ToggleBackpack (ref ContainerFrame.lua l.152-217): the 'B' -- binding (OPENALLBAGS) and the backpack button BOTH open or close EVERY bag at once, not -- just the backpack — the real client's own behavior (MainMenuBarBackpackButton's OnClick and -- the OPENALLBAGS binding both route to ToggleBackpack). "All bags" = the backpack (bag 0, -- which always exists) plus each equipped-bag slot 1..4 that actually holds a bag -- (GetContainerNumSlots > 0); an empty slot has no window to show. The five windows, indexed -- by bag id (BENILLA_BAG_WINDOWS[bagId+1]) — one code path over all of them. BENILLA_BAG_WINDOWS = { "BenillaBagFrame", "BenillaBagFrame1", "BenillaBagFrame2", "BenillaBagFrame3", "BenillaBagFrame4" }
-- THE REFERENCE'S NAMES ARE THE REAL ENTRY POINTS, and our own UI calls THEM. -- -- This is how a 1.12 addon customises anything: it replaces a global and expects the -- client to call its replacement. `Bagnon_Core/core/Overrides.lua` is the canonical shape — -- local bToggleBackpack = ToggleBackpack -- ToggleBackpack = function() ... end -- and until now that override was INERT here, because the 'B' binding and the bag button -- called `BenillaBagToggle_OnClick` directly and nothing ever looked up `ToggleBackpack`. -- Bagnon loaded, appeared in the AddOns list, replaced the globals, and the player still -- got the stock bags. The director saw that; no instrument here could, because the corpus -- survey loads addons and fires events but never CLICKS anything. -- -- The class is far wider than one addon: every "hook a global to change behaviour" addon is -- silently inert wherever our UI calls a benilla-named equivalent instead of the -- reference's name. `CloseAllBags`/`OpenBackpack`/`CloseBackpack` already lived under the -- ref's names in UiPanels.xml for exactly this reason; these are the three that did not. function OpenAllBags() for bagId = 0, 4 do -- The backpack always exists; an equipped-bag slot only when a bag is in it. if bagId == 0 or GetContainerNumSlots(bagId) > 0 then local frame = getglobal(BENILLA_BAG_WINDOWS[bagId + 1]) if frame and not frame:IsShown() then BenillaBagWindow_Repaint(frame) -- bag 0 routes through its observable alias frame:Show() end end end end
-- `ToggleBag(id)` — the ref's per-bag toggle (ContainerFrame.lua l.152-170), and the other -- global Bagnon replaces. Ours drives the same window the all-bags path does. function ToggleBag(id) local frame = getglobal(BENILLA_BAG_WINDOWS[(id or 0) + 1]) if not frame then return end if frame:IsShown() then frame:Hide() else BenillaBagWindow_Repaint(frame) frame:Show() end end
-- `OpenBag(id)` / `CloseBag(id)` / `IsBagOpen(id)` — ToggleBag's three siblings from the -- same reference file (ContainerFrame.lua l.144-185), and the last of that family that was -- still missing here. `Bagnon_Core/core/Overrides.lua` l.42/51 captures BOTH of the first -- two and calls the capture back for any bag Bagnon does not control — a nil call, on the -- ordinary path, for an addon that only *partly* takes the bags over. -- -- The reference's `OpenBag` opens a bag only when `GetContainerNumSlots(id) > 0`; ours keeps -- that gate for 1..4 and exempts bag 0, which always exists (the same rule `OpenAllBags` -- above already applies, for the same reason). function OpenBag(id) id = id or 0 if id ~= 0 and GetContainerNumSlots(id) <= 0 then return end local frame = getglobal(BENILLA_BAG_WINDOWS[id + 1]) if frame and not frame:IsShown() then BenillaBagWindow_Repaint(frame) frame:Show() end end
function CloseBag(id) local frame = getglobal(BENILLA_BAG_WINDOWS[(id or 0) + 1]) if frame and frame:IsShown() then frame:Hide() end end
-- ONE STATED DIVERGENCE. The reference returns the INDEX of the ContainerFrame showing that -- bag (1..NUM_CONTAINER_FRAMES) so its own code can `getglobal("ContainerFrame"..i)`; we -- ship no such pool (each bag has one fixed window), so there is no index to name and this -- answers 1 / nil. Every corpus caller — and the reference's own `ToggleBackpack` — uses it -- as a boolean; a caller that indexed the result would already be reaching for frames that -- do not exist here. function IsBagOpen(id) local frame = getglobal(BENILLA_BAG_WINDOWS[(id or 0) + 1]) if frame and frame:IsShown() then return 1 end return nil end
-- `ToggleBackpack()` — the ref's all-bags toggle ("if numOpen > 0 then CloseAllBags() else -- OpenAllBags()"). It calls the two GLOBALS by name rather than local bodies, so hooking -- either of those works too. function ToggleBackpack() local anyOpen = false for _, name in ipairs(BENILLA_BAG_WINDOWS) do local frame = getglobal(name) if frame and frame:IsShown() then anyOpen = true end end if anyOpen then CloseAllBags() else OpenAllBags() end end
-- The backpack button (MainMenuBarBackpackButton) and the 'B' binding: if any bag window is open, -- close them all; otherwise open every existing bag (ref ToggleBackpack — "if numOpen > 0 -- then CloseAllBags() else OpenAllBags()"). function BenillaBagToggle_OnClick() -- Through the GLOBAL, so an addon that replaced `ToggleBackpack` gets the click. This -- one line is the whole Bagnon fix; the rest below is our own button's checked art, -- which is ours to keep whatever the bag window turns out to be. ToggleBackpack() -- The auto-toggle is provisional (ref BackpackButton_OnClick l.58-67): the button -- lights for the BACKPACK window specifically, whatever the all-toggle just did. local backpack = getglobal(BENILLA_BAG_WINDOWS[1]) getglobal("MainMenuBarBackpackButton"):SetChecked(backpack and backpack:IsShown()) end
-- The window's bar button (ref ContainerFrame_OnShow/OnHide: bag 0 → -- MainMenuBarBackpackButton, bags 1..4 → CharacterBag(N-1)Slot). function BenillaBagWindow_BarButton(frame) local name = frame:GetName() if name == "BenillaKeyRingFrame" then return getglobal("KeyRingButton") end for bagId = 0, 4 do if name == BENILLA_BAG_WINDOWS[bagId + 1] then if bagId == 0 then return getglobal("MainMenuBarBackpackButton") end return getglobal("CharacterBag" .. (bagId - 1) .. "Slot") end end end
-- Open/close sounds — the window-sound convention (decision 0090), wrapper form: a named -- Benilla<Window>Frame_OnShow/_OnHide fn (used when the handler is more than the bare -- PlaySound, or — as here — to carry the cite). Kits quoted from the real ContainerFrame.lua -- ContainerFrame_OnShow/OnHide (l.124-142 / l.100-122), reused VERBATIM by every window -- (backpack included), INCLUDING the real fn's keyring fork: the keyring has its own -- jingling KeyRingOpen/KeyRingClose pair (both real SoundEntries kits), every other window -- the plain igBackPackOpen/igBackPackClose. Fired on every visibility transition (a Show/Hide -- from a toggle button, the 'B' binding, a close button, or ESC), never at load (every window -- is authored hidden="true", so none ever transitions on startup). -- -- The `this` legacy global (RF-0025, script/event.rs) names the window that just -- shown/hidden — used here for the open-window STACK the layout law below reads, rather -- than a per-window OnShow/OnHide body (which would defeat the whole point of sharing one -- handler across five windows). function BenillaBagFrame_OnShow() if this:GetID() == KEYRING_CONTAINER then PlaySound("KeyRingOpen") else PlaySound("igBackPackOpen") end -- The bar lights the open bag's button (ref ContainerFrame_OnShow l.124-131, -- SetChecked(1)) — the window side is the source of truth, so a bag opened by any -- path (the B key, a bar click, open-all at a vendor) lights its button. local barButton = BenillaBagWindow_BarButton(this) if barButton then barButton:SetChecked(1) end BenillaBagStack_Open(this) end
function BenillaBagFrame_OnHide() if this:GetID() == KEYRING_CONTAINER then PlaySound("KeyRingClose") else PlaySound("igBackPackClose") end -- ...and clears it on any close (ref ContainerFrame_OnHide l.84-95, SetChecked(0)). local barButton = BenillaBagWindow_BarButton(this) if barButton then barButton:SetChecked(0) end BenillaBagStack_Close(this) end
-- ── The open-bag stack + layout law (ref ContainerFrame1.bags + -- updateContainerFrameAnchors, ContainerFrame.lua:472-552, transcribed shape) ───────────── -- Open windows stack bottom-right UPWARD in show order: the first at the backpack's own -- anchor (BOTTOMRIGHT, x=0/y=70 — CONTAINER_OFFSET_X/Y), each next one anchored above the -- previous (TOPRIGHT → BOTTOMRIGHT, CONTAINER_SPACING=0 gap); when a stack would run off the -- top of the screen, the NEXT window starts a fresh column one CONTAINER_WIDTH further left. -- Out of scope (nothing here ever needs it): the ref's UI-scale/BankFrame-collision shrink -- branch (l.505-539) — benilla has no uiScale CVar and no bank window yet. BENILLA_BAG_STACK = {} local BENILLA_CONTAINER_OFFSET_X = 0 local BENILLA_CONTAINER_OFFSET_Y = 70 local BENILLA_CONTAINER_WIDTH = 192 local BENILLA_CONTAINER_SPACING = 0 local BENILLA_VISIBLE_CONTAINER_SPACING = 3
function BenillaBagStack_Open(frame) table.insert(BENILLA_BAG_STACK, frame) BenillaBagStack_Relayout() end
function BenillaBagStack_Close(frame) for i = 1, table.getn(BENILLA_BAG_STACK) do if BENILLA_BAG_STACK[i] == frame then table.remove(BENILLA_BAG_STACK, i) break end end BenillaBagStack_Relayout() end
function BenillaBagStack_Relayout() local screenHeight = GetScreenHeight() local freeHeight = screenHeight - BENILLA_CONTAINER_OFFSET_Y local column = 0 for i = 1, table.getn(BENILLA_BAG_STACK) do local frame = BENILLA_BAG_STACK[i] if i == 1 then frame:SetPoint("BOTTOMRIGHT", -BENILLA_CONTAINER_OFFSET_X, BENILLA_CONTAINER_OFFSET_Y) elseif freeHeight < frame:GetHeight() then column = column + 1 freeHeight = screenHeight - BENILLA_CONTAINER_OFFSET_Y frame:SetPoint("BOTTOMRIGHT", -(column * BENILLA_CONTAINER_WIDTH) - BENILLA_CONTAINER_OFFSET_X, BENILLA_CONTAINER_OFFSET_Y) else frame:SetPoint("BOTTOMRIGHT", BENILLA_BAG_STACK[i - 1], "TOPRIGHT", 0, BENILLA_CONTAINER_SPACING) end freeHeight = freeHeight - frame:GetHeight() - BENILLA_VISIBLE_CONTAINER_SPACING end end
-- ── The bag bar (decision 0216 slice 2) — four 30×30 buttons left of MainMenuBarBackpackButton, -- mirroring the reference main-bar bag buttons (CharacterBag0..3Slot). No exact reference -- XML was available to transcribe (not in the session's extracted set) — size (30×30) and -- placement (left of the backpack button) are per the brief; inter-button spacing is an -- authored assumption (2px), FLAGGED for the director's look. Each button shows the -- equipped bag's own icon (GetInventoryItemTexture, inv slots 20..23 — Bag0Slot..Bag3Slot, -- PaperDollItemFrame.dbc-verified, decision 0216 slice 2's char-feed extension) or the -- empty-slot art when no bag is equipped there. Click toggles that bag's window — NAMED -- DEFERRAL: no drag-to-equip a bag onto the bar yet (that's the paper-doll drag arc, slice -- 3's scope, not this one). -- The bag bar (and the backpack toggle) are RELOCATED onto the action bar — anchored into -- MainMenuBarArtFrame's bottom-right — which means they need seating one frame level -- above the bar art or it paints over their icons. That lever lives with the frame it's -- about: BenillaActionBarArt_SeatAbove (ActionBar.xml, loaded before this file), which -- carries the full explanation; the micro-button row is its second caller. Called -- nil-GUARDED here: the shipped load order always has the bar first, but ~25 bag/bank/ -- escape/merchant test harnesses load THIS file alone — and with no bar loaded there is by -- definition no bar art to seat above, so the guard's no-op is the right answer, not a -- swallowed failure.
-- Bag0Slot..Bag3Slot = live inv ids 20..23 (char_stats.rs SLOT_INFO, DBC-verified); OUR bag -- ids 1..4 map the same way (bagId N ⇒ inv slot 19+N), the id PickupInventoryItem/ -- GetInventoryItemTexture speak. function BenillaBagBarSlot_InvSlot(button) return 19 + button.bagId end
function BenillaBagBarSlot_OnLoad(button, bagId) button.bagId = bagId -- The button's ID is the REFERENCE's: its 1-based inventory slot, 20..23 (the real -- client gets there through PaperDollItemSlotButton_OnLoad, which resolves -- "CharacterBag0Slot" → "Bag0Slot" → GetInventorySlotInfo → 20). Nothing of ours reads -- it — every body here goes through `button.bagId` — but every ADDON does: -- `Bagnon.lua:104` computes its highlight target as `this:GetID() - 19`, and against -- an unset id that is -19, so Bagnon highlighted the wrong bag (silently, with no -- raise) on every bag-slot hover. `isBag` is the same story from the same template -- (ref BagSlotButtonTemplate OnLoad l.33), read by KeyRingItemButton_OnClick. button:SetID(19 + bagId) button.isBag = 1 button.icon = getglobal(button:GetName() .. "IconTexture") if BenillaActionBarArt_SeatAbove then BenillaActionBarArt_SeatAbove(button) end -- Both buttons (ref BagSlotButtonTemplate inherits PaperDollItemSlotButtonTemplate, and -- its OnLoad calls PaperDollItemSlotButton_OnLoad — PaperDollFrame.lua:86 — so a bag-bar -- slot registers the pair like every doll slot; MainMenuBarBagButtons.xml:78 does the -- same for the backpack). BagSlotButton_OnClick reads no button: right-click opens the -- bag, exactly as left does. button:RegisterForClicks("LeftButtonUp", "RightButtonUp") -- Drag-to-equip (decision 0208 phase 1b's deferred bag-icon arm, now landed): the bar -- slot is a paper-doll equipment slot for bags. LEFT drag picks the equipped bag up; -- a drag/receive drops a carried bag in to equip it (PickupInventoryItem — the exact -- doll-slot transition, the app maps id 20..23 onto wire bag slots 19..22). button:RegisterForDrag("LeftButton") button:RegisterEvent("UNIT_INVENTORY_CHANGED") button:RegisterEvent("BAG_UPDATE") button:RegisterEvent("ITEM_LOCK_CHANGED") BenillaBagBarSlot_Update(button) end
-- Placing/equipping a carried bag (or picking the equipped one up) rides PickupInventoryItem, -- exactly like a paper-doll slot; the empty-cursor plain click just toggles the bag's window. function BenillaBagBarSlot_Place(button) PickupInventoryItem(BenillaBagBarSlot_InvSlot(button)) BenillaBagBarSlot_Update(button) end
function BenillaBagBarSlot_OnClick(button) if CursorHasItem() then BenillaBagBarSlot_Place(button) -- drop/equip the carried bag onto this slot else local frame = getglobal("BenillaBagFrame" .. button.bagId) if frame then if frame:IsShown() then frame:Hide() else BenillaBagWindow_Update(frame) frame:Show() end end end -- The click's own CheckButton auto-toggle is provisional — re-derive from the -- window on every branch, the ref's exact tail (BagSlotButton_OnClick l.12-20: -- SetChecked(isVisible) whether the click toggled, placed a bag, or did nothing). local frame = getglobal("BenillaBagFrame" .. button.bagId) button:SetChecked(frame and frame:IsShown()) end
function BenillaBagBarSlot_OnEvent(button) if event == "UNIT_INVENTORY_CHANGED" and arg1 ~= "player" then return end -- ITEM_LOCK_CHANGED names its slot in arg1/arg2; the bar's slots are the EQUIPMENT_BAG -- space, so a bag-window lock event (a real bag id in arg1) never concerns the icon — -- repainting anyway is idempotent (the lock read below is slot-specific). BAG_UPDATE -- fires per-bag-CONTENTS change, not per-icon change (the icon is the bag ITEM's own -- texture) — repainting on it too covers the freshly-equipped-bag-template-in-flight frame. BenillaBagBarSlot_Update(button) end
-- ── The bar buttons' hovers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- ref GlobalStrings.lua l.132 / l.1458 (enUS), fallback form: the real localized -- GlobalStrings.lua runs before this file at runtime (ui_script/mod.rs), so these only -- fill in for the harnesses that load no patch chain. BACKPACK_TOOLTIP = BACKPACK_TOOLTIP or "Backpack" EQUIP_CONTAINER = EQUIP_CONTAINER or "Equip Container" -- ref GlobalStrings.lua l.2472 / l.2810 — the keyring's window title + button tooltip, and -- the full-keyring refusal. KEYRING = KEYRING or "Keyring" NO_EMPTY_KEYRING_SLOTS_ERROR = NO_EMPTY_KEYRING_SLOTS_ERROR or "Your keyring is full."
-- Both are PLAIN tooltips — the reference calls GameTooltip:SetText here, not -- GameTooltip_AddNewbieTip, so unlike the micro buttons next door (0661) there is no second -- explanation line to be missing. They also anchor beside the button (ANCHOR_LEFT, so the -- plate opens toward screen center off a bottom-right button), NOT at the default corner. -- -- ref MainMenuBarBackpackButton OnEnter (ref-MainMenuBarBagButtons.xml l.91-99). The ref -- appends the live binding key with GameTooltip:AppendText; ours concatenates the same -- suffix from a LIVE GetBindingKey read since 0997 (our one bag knob is OPENALLBAGS — -- the toggle this very button runs), rendered through the Key Bindings window's display -- law when it is loaded. Unbound: the bare label, the ref's own read. function BenillaBagToggle_OnEnter(button) if not GameTooltip then return end -- engine tests load file subsets GameTooltip:SetOwner(button, "ANCHOR_LEFT") local text = BACKPACK_TOOLTIP local key = GetBindingKey("OPENALLBAGS") if key then if KeyBindings_KeyText then key = KeyBindings_KeyText(key) end text = text .. " " .. NORMAL_FONT_COLOR_CODE .. "(" .. key .. ")" .. FONT_COLOR_CODE_CLOSE end GameTooltip:SetText(text, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0) end
-- ref BagSlotButton_OnEnter (ref-MainMenuBarBagButtons.lua l.86-96): the equipped bag's own -- item tooltip, or "Equip Container" for an empty slot. The ref's "(F1)".."(F4)" suffix -- needs GetBindingKey AND the TOGGLEBAG1..4 bindings — benilla ships neither, so no slot -- carries one; the day those bind, this is where the suffix goes. function BenillaBagBarSlot_OnEnter(button) if not GameTooltip then return end GameTooltip:SetOwner(button, "ANCHOR_LEFT") if not GameTooltip:SetInventoryItem("player", BenillaBagBarSlot_InvSlot(button)) then GameTooltip:SetText(EQUIP_CONTAINER, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0) end end
-- `BagSlotButton_OnEnter()` — THE REFERENCE'S NAME for the hover above, and the entry point -- the four `CharacterBag<N>Slot` buttons actually call (their XML below). Published for the -- same standing reason `ToggleBackpack` is: an addon replaces the client's global and -- expects the client to call the replacement. -- -- `Bagnon.lua:67` is the exact shape, and it is a hover-frequency call, not a rare one: -- bBagSlotButton_OnEnter = BagSlotButton_OnEnter -- capture ours -- BagSlotButton_OnEnter = BagnonBlizBag_OnEnter -- replace the global -- Bagnon's replacement highlights the matching slots in its own window and then calls the -- capture. With the global absent that capture was nil, and — because nothing here ever -- looked the global up — the replacement was never reached to raise on it: Bagnon's -- highlight was simply, silently inert. Corpus demand is exactly one addon (this one) at -- two sites; its siblings `BagSlotButton_OnClick`/`_OnDrag`/`_OnShiftClick`/ -- `BackpackButton_OnClick` score ZERO and are deliberately not published (1210). -- -- The reference's body takes no argument and reads `this`; so does this one. function BagSlotButton_OnEnter() BenillaBagBarSlot_OnEnter(this) end
-- ref OnLeave for both (l.100-102 / the template's own): a plain Hide, no fade — the item -- half of the split BenillaUnitFrame_OnLeave's comment describes. function BenillaBagBarButton_OnLeave() if GameTooltip then GameTooltip:Hide() end end
-- ── The keyring (decision 0765) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- ref ToggleKeyRing (ContainerFrame.lua:757-771). The reference generates the window on -- demand from a pool of generic ContainerFrames sized to GetKeyRingSize(); ours is a fixed -- window like the other six, so the toggle is the bag bar's own show/hide shape and the -- size arrives through the feed. The ref's IsOptionFrameOpen() guard has no analogue here -- (our bag-bar buttons carry none either — the game menu greys the row instead, 0674), and -- its SetButtonPulse stop is moot with no pulse to stop (0304). function ToggleKeyRing() local frame = getglobal("BenillaKeyRingFrame") if not frame then return end if frame:IsShown() then frame:Hide() else BenillaBagWindow_Update(frame) frame:Show() end end
-- ref PutKeyInKeyRing (ContainerFrame.lua:740-755) — dropping a held key onto the keyring -- BUTTON files it in the first free slot. "Pick up" from an empty slot IS the place gesture -- (PickupContainerItem is the one entry point: empty cursor picks up, a held cursor places), -- which is why the reference's own line reads as a pickup. -- -- One deliberate un-quirking: the ref passes `NO_EMPTY_KEYRING_SLOTS`, but GlobalStrings -- only ever defined `NO_EMPTY_KEYRING_SLOTS_ERROR` — so the real client silently prints -- nothing when your keyring is full. We print the string that exists. function PutKeyInKeyRing() for i = 1, GetKeyRingSize() do -- Occupancy is `texture or itemCount`, not `texture` alone. The reference tests -- the texture (ContainerFrame_Update) because ITS client always has the icon by -- the time a slot is populated; ours can hold an item whose icon has not resolved -- yet, and reading that as an empty slot would file the key on top of it -- (decision 1199 — the transient our five-value shape exposed). local texture, itemCount = GetContainerItemInfo(KEYRING_CONTAINER, i) if texture == nil and itemCount == nil then PickupContainerItem(KEYRING_CONTAINER, i) return end end if UIErrorsFrame then UIErrorsFrame:AddMessage(NO_EMPTY_KEYRING_SLOTS_ERROR, 1.0, 0.1, 0.1) end end
-- ref KeyRingButton's OnLoad/OnClick/OnReceiveDrag (MainMenuBarBagButtons.xml l.142-199). -- The button is authored HIDDEN and only ever revealed by MainMenuBar_UpdateKeyRing -- (ActionBar.xml), which is where the whole show/hide law and its divergence note live. function BenillaKeyRingButton_OnLoad(button) button:SetID(KEYRING_CONTAINER) button:RegisterForClicks("LeftButtonUp", "RightButtonUp") button:RegisterForDrag("LeftButton") -- The ref watches PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD / VARIABLES_LOADED / BAG_UPDATE on the bar's art -- frame; with no saved variable there is nothing for VARIABLES_LOADED to restore, and -- BAG_UPDATE is what actually carries "a key just arrived". button:RegisterEvent("PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD") button:RegisterEvent("BAG_UPDATE") if BenillaActionBarArt_SeatAbove then BenillaActionBarArt_SeatAbove(button) end BenillaKeyRingButton_OnEvent() end
function BenillaKeyRingButton_OnEvent() if MainMenuBar_UpdateKeyRing then MainMenuBar_UpdateKeyRing() end end
function BenillaKeyRingButton_OnClick(button) -- Holding something ⇒ file it; empty-handed ⇒ open/close the keyring (ref l.166-173). if CursorHasItem() then PutKeyInKeyRing() else ToggleKeyRing() end -- Re-derive the lit ring from the window, the same provisional-toggle tail every other -- bag-bar button uses. local frame = getglobal("BenillaKeyRingFrame") button:SetChecked(frame and frame:IsShown()) end
-- ref l.180-184: the plain KEYRING title plus the ref's own empty AddLine (which reserves -- the second row the binding key would print into — we ship no TOGGLEKEYRING binding, the -- same gap the bag slots' "(F1)".."(F4)" suffixes have). function BenillaKeyRingButton_OnEnter(button) if not GameTooltip then return end GameTooltip:SetOwner(button, "ANCHOR_LEFT") GameTooltip:SetText(KEYRING, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0) end
function BenillaBagBarSlot_Update(button) local invSlot = BenillaBagBarSlot_InvSlot(button) local texture = GetInventoryItemTexture("player", invSlot) button.icon:SetTexture(texture or "Interface\\PaperDoll\\UI-PaperDoll-Slot-Bag") -- Dim while the bag is up on the cursor or a pending equip is in flight (the doll's own -- drag feedback, IsInventoryItemLocked — the bag-slot twin of BenillaBagSlot_Update). if IsInventoryItemLocked(invSlot) then button.icon:SetVertexColor(0.4, 0.4, 0.4) elseif button:IsEnabled() then button.icon:SetVertexColor(1, 1, 1) else -- Disabled by Disable_BagButtons below: keep the grey. The reference needs no such -- arm — its desaturation is a shader flag on the texture, untouched by an Update -- that only re-sets the image — but ours IS a vertex colour (UiPanels.xml -- SetDesaturation), so a bag update behind the open game menu would otherwise -- repaint the icon bright under a button that stayed dead. button.icon:SetVertexColor(0.5, 0.5, 0.5) end end
-- ── The item-push drop animation (decision 0887) ───────────────────────────────────────── -- An item lands in a bag: its icon pops in above the bag bar, hangs there, then falls into -- the button that took it and shrinks away. ref ItemAnim (MainMenuBarBagButtons.xml l.4-16 + -- .lua l.68-80, .lua l.92-94): each bag button owns a hidden child that, on ITEM_PUSH -- naming its own container, swaps in the pushed item's icon, rewinds to sequence time 0 and -- shows itself; OnAnimFinished hides it again. A second push on the same button RESTARTS it -- (SetSequenceTime(0,0)); pushes into different bags run independently. That is exactly the -- machine below, with the reference's ITEM_PUSH `arg1` translated from its inventory-slot -- vocabulary (20..23) into ours (bagId 1..4) app-side — ui_loot.rs `push_container` carries -- the byte-verified selector. -- -- The reference's is a <Model> playing Interface\ItemAnimations\ForcedBackpackItem.mdx — a -- single 4-vertex quad on one animated bone, i.e. a 2D icon card with keyframed scale, alpha -- and offset. benilla has no Model widget (decision 0137's Cooldown took the same posture: -- model the mechanism, let our own renderer draw it), so it is a Texture driven by the -- model's OWN tracks, read out of the shipped .m2 with `benilla-extract m2anim`/`m2bones`: -- -- sequence 0, CLAMP (plays once), duration 1.000 s -- texture-weight (alpha) 0.000→0.0 0.133→1.0 0.267→1.0 1.000→0.0 linear -- bone 0 scale 0.000→1.0 0.133→1.2 0.267→1.0 1.000→0.014 linear -- bone 0 translation 0.000→(0,0) 0.500→(0,0) 1.000→(+0.010,-0.040) -- the quad itself: 0.03 x 0.03 model units, blend Alpha, unlit, no depth write -- -- So: fade in over the first 133 ms while swelling to 1.2x; settle back to full size by -- 267 ms; from there dwindle and fade continuously for the remaining 733 ms — while the -- POSITION holds until the half-second and only then falls. The three tracks deliberately -- do not share a schedule: the card is already down to ~0.69 size and ~0.68 alpha when it -- starts moving, so the drop reads as the icon being drawn into the bag rather than as a -- solid tile sliding. Those numbers are the file's, not ours. -- -- THE ONE AUTHORED NUMBER is the model-unit → pixel scale, because a <Model> frame's 3D -- projection is not RE-recorded (the ref's ItemAnim frame has no <Size> at all, so the rect -- cannot be it) — see decision 0887's named gap. 1200 px/unit is the sibling calibration: -- CooldownFrameTemplate is the same kind of degenerate UI model, its four quads span 0.04 -- units, and at its scale="0.75" that sweep covers a 36px action button ⇒ 0.04·K·0.75 = 36. -- At K = 1200 this model's own numbers land on 36 px of icon (exactly a bag-bar button), -- a 48 px fall and a 12 px sideways drift — which is why the sizes below are stated as the -- model's ratios times the icon, not as free pixels: correct the scale in one place and the -- whole animation stays in proportion. BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_PX_PER_UNIT = 1200 BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_DURATION = 1.0 BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_SIZE = 0.03 * BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_PX_PER_UNIT -- 36 BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_FALL = 0.04 * BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_PX_PER_UNIT -- 48 BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_DRIFT = 0.01 * BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_PX_PER_UNIT -- 12 -- {time, value} keyframes, linear between (M2 track interpolation 1) — the file's own keys. BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_ALPHA = { {0.000, 0.0}, {0.133, 1.0}, {0.267, 1.0}, {1.000, 0.0} } BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_SCALE = { {0.000, 1.0}, {0.133, 1.2}, {0.267, 1.0}, {1.000, 0.014} } -- The translation track as a 0..1 fraction of the fall (both components move together, so -- one curve drives both axes — the file keys (0,0) at 0.000 and 0.500, the full offset at -- 1.000, i.e. it hangs for the first half second and then drops). BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_DROP = { {0.000, 0.0}, {0.500, 0.0}, {1.000, 1.0} }
-- Sample a {time, value} keyframe list at `t`, linear between keys, clamped at both ends -- (the M2 sampler's own shape for a CLAMP sequence). function BenillaItemPushAnim_Sample(track, t) local last = table.getn(track) if t <= track[1][1] then return track[1][2] end for i = 2, last do local key = track[i] if t <= key[1] then local prev = track[i - 1] local span = key[1] - prev[1] if span <= 0 then return key[2] end return prev[2] + (key[2] - prev[2]) * (t - prev[1]) / span end end return track[last][2] end
-- Place/size/fade the card for the current clock. The card LANDS centred on its button and -- STARTS a fall's height above it (and a drift's width to the left), so the icon reads as -- floating clear above the bar and then dropping into the bag — the model's own relative -- motion, anchored to the button rather than to the ref's unresolvable model origin. function BenillaItemPushAnim_Paint(anim) local t = anim.elapsed local drop = BenillaItemPushAnim_Sample(BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_DROP, t) local size = BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_SIZE * BenillaItemPushAnim_Sample(BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_SCALE, t) anim:SetWidth(size) anim:SetHeight(size) anim:SetPoint("CENTER", anim:GetParent(), "CENTER", BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_DRIFT * (drop - 1), BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_FALL * (1 - drop)) anim:SetAlpha(BenillaItemPushAnim_Sample(BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_ALPHA, t)) end
-- ref ItemAnim_OnLoad (l.68-70): the card listens for ITEM_PUSH and nothing else. It is -- authored hidden, so it costs no OnUpdate until a push shows it (events reach hidden -- frames; OnUpdate does not — the reference's own split). function BenillaItemPushAnim_OnLoad(anim, containerId) anim.containerId = containerId anim.icon = getglobal(anim:GetName() .. "Icon") anim.elapsed = 0 anim:RegisterEvent("ITEM_PUSH") end
-- ref ItemAnim_OnEvent (l.72-80): `if this:GetParent():GetID() == arg1`, then -- ReplaceIconTexture(arg2) / SetSequence(0) / SetSequenceTime(0,0) / Show. A push into a bag -- with no button (a bank bag) matches nothing and animates nowhere, there and here. function BenillaItemPushAnim_OnEvent(anim) if arg1 ~= anim.containerId then return end anim.icon:SetTexture(arg2) anim.elapsed = 0 -- Seat the card above its button rather than at load: the bag bar's own level is set in -- the BUTTON's OnLoad (BenillaActionBarArt_SeatAbove), which the loader may run after -- this child exists. Re-deriving it per push is one call and can never read it stale. anim:SetFrameLevel(anim:GetParent():GetFrameLevel() + 1) BenillaItemPushAnim_Paint(anim) anim:Show() end
-- The CLAMP sequence's end is the ref's OnAnimFinished → this:Hide() (l.92-94). function BenillaItemPushAnim_OnUpdate(anim, elapsed) anim.elapsed = anim.elapsed + (elapsed or 0) if anim.elapsed >= BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_DURATION then anim:Hide() return end BenillaItemPushAnim_Paint(anim) end
-- The bag BAR's five buttons (the backpack toggle + the four equipped-bag slots) — the row -- Disable_/Enable_BagButtons greys as a unit. Distinct from UiPanels.xml's BAG_WINDOWS, -- which is the five bag *windows* those buttons open. BENILLA_BAG_BUTTONS = { "MainMenuBarBackpackButton", "CharacterBag0Slot", "CharacterBag1Slot", "CharacterBag2Slot", "CharacterBag3Slot" }
-- Disable_BagButtons / Enable_BagButtons — ref MainMenuBarBagButtons.lua l.102-128, called -- by GameMenuFrame's OnShow/OnHide (decision 0674) and by nothing else: while the game menu -- holds the screen, the whole bag row greys out. That is the *visible* half of a rule the -- panel manager already enforces (ShowUIPanel's native-center gate refuses every window -- while the menu is up — UiPanels.xml `CanOpenPanels`); without it the bags would look -- clickable and simply do nothing. -- -- Mapping onto benilla's row: the ref's MainMenuBarBackpackButton is MainMenuBarBackpackButton and -- CharacterBag0..3Slot are CharacterBag0Slot..4 — and in BOTH cases the greying goes onto -- the button's `$parentIcon` LAYER texture, never onto a state texture. That is the -- reference's own structure and it is load-bearing here: a disabled button draws its -- DisabledTexture, and with none set it draws no state texture at all -- (`ButtonState::region_visible`), so greying a NormalTexture would grey something already -- gone. The four slots' UI-Quickslot2 rings ARE state textures and do vanish while -- disabled unless the slot states one explicitly — so what you should see is the -- ring stay put and the bag icon grey — which is why each slot repeats its ring as -- DisabledTexture (see the slot instances below). function Disable_BagButtons() for _, button in ipairs(BENILLA_BAG_BUTTONS) do local b = getglobal(button) b:Disable() SetDesaturation(b.icon, 1) end end
function Enable_BagButtons() for _, button in ipairs(BENILLA_BAG_BUTTONS) do local b = getglobal(button) b:Enable() SetDesaturation(b.icon, nil) end -- The four slots' own paint decides their restored colour: an item locked on the cursor -- wants 0.4 grey, not the flat white SetDesaturation(nil) just left. for i = 1, 4 do BenillaBagBarSlot_Update(getglobal("CharacterBag" .. (i - 1) .. "Slot")) end end

Scripts.OnLoad: self.icon = getglobal("MainMenuBarBackpackButtonIconTexture") if BenillaActionBarArt_SeatAbove then BenillaActionBarArt_SeatAbove(self) end
